title: Section 9 names persons as decision owners
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4
section: 9 Open decisions that change these requirements
description: Four rows of the open-decision table give the decision owner as a person: DL06, DL12, DL13 and DL20. The run forbids person names in any output, so the four owner cells are replaced by the value placeholder and the role cannot be stated without inventing one.
evidence: DL06 owner cell names two persons; DL12 owner cell names two persons; DL13 owner cell names one person together with TechX and Henka; DL20 owner cell names the solution architect with one person.
proposed: Confirm the role that owns each of DL06, DL12, DL13 and DL20 and record the role, not the person, in the decision log.

title: One requirement prefix, REQ-DRI, is used by two modules
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4
description: REQ-DRI-006, 007, 008 and 013 are written under P2 Integration, and REQ-DRI-001 to 005 and 009 to 012 under P7 Decision center and log. A single prefix therefore maps to two services, so a requirement ID alone does not say which service delivers it.
evidence: Section 5.2 table carries REQ-DRI-006, REQ-DRI-007, REQ-DRI-008 and REQ-DRI-013; section 5.7 table carries REQ-DRI-001 to REQ-DRI-005 and REQ-DRI-009 to REQ-DRI-012.
proposed: Keep the IDs stable. Resolve the service from the section the requirement sits in, and record the split in the traceability matrix.

title: No delivery model or service-epic mapping in version 4
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4
description: Version 4 states the requirements against the single-service ACE module. It has no service epic, no wave and no contract-first build order, so nothing in the BRD says which of the 19 services delivers a requirement.
evidence: Sections 1 to 9 contain no service epic code, no wave number and no contract reference.
proposed: Added as section 10 Delivery model and section 11 trace table under D-RCV-60.

title: Business epic codes EP01 to EP08 are not defined in this document
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4
description: The realignment tags every story with a business epic EP01 to EP08, but the BRD names the eight epics E1 to E8 only. The correspondence between the two code sets is not stated anywhere in the source.
evidence: Section 8 lists E1 to E8 with a release date and a theme; no EP code appears in the document.
proposed: State the mapping EP01 to EP08 equal to E1 to E8 in the delivery model, and carry it in the story masters.

title: Three constraints in section 7 contradict the target architecture
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4
description: The rows Built on ACE, Modular monolith and Programmatic workflow state one service and one repository, a modular monolith and an explicitly programmatic workflow with no Temporal. D-RCV-60 adopts 19 services inside ACE, one schema and login per service, and a reusable Temporal layer, so the three rows cannot stand word for word.
evidence: Section 7 row Built on ACE reads one service, one repository, one front end; row Modular monolith reads common, collection and recovery modules; row Programmatic workflow reads no Temporal.
proposed: Restate the three rows in version 5 as superseded by D-RCV-60 and ADR-013, ADR-014 and ADR-016, and keep every other constraint unchanged.

title: Interaction ledger requirements sit under P7 but the ledger is P1's
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4
description: REQ-ILG-001 to REQ-ILG-014 are written in the P7 section, while the source precedence default ruling and DP-18 give the interaction ledger to P1 rwb-source-data, and the Ownership Map rules the interaction table to P1. The requirement text is right; only the section and the delivering service disagree.
evidence: Section 5.7 table carries the fourteen REQ-ILG rows; Ownership Map Rulings sheet rules interaction to P1; R-PREC default ruling names P1 rwb-source-data for the interaction ledger.
proposed: Keep the IDs and the text where they are. Deliver the ledger under RWB-SVC-P1 and note the split in the delivery model.

title: Approval requirements sit under P7 but the authority table is P4's
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4
description: REQ-ACA-004 and REQ-APD-001 to REQ-APD-011 read the delegation of authority table. The Ownership Map rules the delegation table to P4 rwb-access, while the approval requirements are written under P7. No requirement states which service holds the table.
evidence: REQ-ACA-004 is written in section 5.4; the REQ-APD rows are written in section 5.7; Ownership Map Rulings sheet rules delegation_limit to P4.
proposed: Deliver the approvals under RWB-SVC-P7 against P4's authority table, and state that in the delivery model and in the API contract.

title: No requirement section for P8 payment, P9 reporting or P10 agent
source: Recovery Workbench Business Requirements Program v4
description: Section 5 has sixteen sections: P1 to P7 and S1 to S9. P8 payment, P9 reporting and P10 agent have no section of their own, so their duties are only stated inside other sections, and no requirement ID can be traced to them.
evidence: Section 5 headings run 5.1 P1 to 5.7 P7 and 5.8 S1 to 5.16 S9; no 5.x section names P8, P9 or P10.
proposed: Add the three service epics to the delivery model with no requirement row, and let the service PRD carry their requirements until a later version adds the sections.
